narrative_purpose: The cold-open anchor: a colossal flier at the instant of launch off a high crag, posed so its impossible scale and its cliff-vault launch - the very strategy a too-heavy flier must use - read immediately.
subject: A great leonopteryx (toruk) at the instant of launch from the edge of a floating mountain: enormous fore-wings swept back mid-downstroke, a second smaller pair of limbs held out as horizontal stabilisers, taloned hind feet still trailing the rock it has just pushed off. The wings are vast finned membranes, crimson-and-orange shading to dark, faint glow along the wing struts. Far below and behind, a tiny banshee with its rider wheels in the open air for scale, dwarfed by the toruk's span.
scene: The lip of a floating island-mountain, mist and forest canopy falling away into deep hazy distance below, other drifting peaks behind.
camera: A dramatic low three-quarter view looking slightly up at the launching toruk, the cliff edge and the void beneath it visible, the distant rider small.
light: Cool hazy daylight, a warm rim of amber-crimson along the wing leading edges, deep indigo shadow in the membrane folds and the gulf below.
palette: Void-indigo and teal sky-haze, crimson-and-amber on the toruk's wings, cool grey rock, scarce cyan glow on the struts.
style: Painterly cinematic naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, strong focal drama.
detail_level: Crisp on the toruk's wings, stabiliser limbs, and the trailing feet; the cliff and distant rider softer; deep haze below.
composition: The toruk dominating the upper two-thirds with wings spread wide, the cliff edge lower-left, the void and tiny rider lower-right, generous dark sky for text, 16:9.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette with a warm wing accent. Same dark glowing mood as the chapter cover; reuse the cover's banshee look for the distant rider.
